spec_match.rationale: Each step paraphrases a cited source: the ChromeStatus summary (ESB-only, text sent only on high-confidence indicators, ephemeral processing), the 2025 blog (on-device predecessor) and features.cc/csd.proto (MaxIntelligentScansPerDayDesktop=5 source default, NoInfoReason values, model_type).

interactive.rationale: Radios, checkboxes and a number input rebuild the step list; Prev/Next and clickable steps move aria-current; the data ledger table updates.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature index card describes exactly what the page does, including that it is a labelled model / manual observation where applicable.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers level 0/1, no indicators, too-short text, quota exhaustion, server unavailable, on-device unavailable, and the 137-154 vs 155 migration.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5094379441225728 plus the Chromium source or blog sources used.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's manual assertions (ESB gating, data minimisation, model swap) point at this page as the observation route and are honestly reported as blocked; no fake probe.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 153 (Playwright CDP) at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 touch. chrome-devtools-mcp is NOT available in this environment, so there is no DevTools-MCP verification and no accessibility-tree dump. Driven through all levels, both pipelines, quota at 5, the unavailable and short-text toggles, and Next to the end; step lists and ledger changed as expected. A 139px mobile overflow (implicit grid track sized by the step buttons' min-content) was found, fixed with grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr), and re-measured at 0px. Only the 2 expected panel warnings appeared.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts scam-flow-text-upload-only-when-gated: the 'Page text is sent' step appears iff ESB + indicators + text + server pipeline + quota remaining.

design_system.rationale: Only public/styles.css tokens; buttons that override background also set color; status colours (emerald-dark, rose) used only on light backgrounds.

accessibility.rationale: Native controls with labels, fieldset/legend, polite live regions and visible focus. However, the accessibility tree was not inspected with chrome-devtools-mcp, which is unavailable here.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Exercised at 360x740 DPR3 touch and 1280x800: 0px horizontal overflow on both after the final edit, single-column layout on mobile, 44px targets.

openQuestions.title: Confirm whether Standard users get any server scan on desktop
openQuestions.detail: kClientSideDetectionOnlyESBClassification exists; reading client_side_detection_host.cc would confirm the exact ESB gate and whether Standard profiles run any local classification that feeds this path.

openQuestions.title: Track the live quota value
openQuestions.detail: 5 is only the source default of MaxIntelligentScansPerDayDesktop; Finch configs may differ. Re-check when Google documents the desktop rollout.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use aria-live polite for standard status updates, reserve assertive for critical ones; label every control; visible focus; 24px+ targets (bumped to 44px here).
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Readouts and verdicts are aria-live polite (never assertive); all inputs are inside <label>; :focus-visible 3px outline; buttons/labels min-height 44px.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use visible radio buttons for 1-5 exclusive options, native checkboxes for multi-select, label every input, use aria-describedby for hints.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All exclusive choices (level, mode, platform, pipeline) are native radio groups in fieldset/legend; hints linked with aria-describedby.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Multi-step flows should expose the current step and keep controls operable; use native buttons.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Steps are native buttons in an ordered list with aria-current=step; Prev/Next use aria-disabled rather than disabled so focus is not lost at either end; the position text is polite-live.

summary: Sourced, accessible stepper showing exactly when page text leaves the device.
